subject: Equinox Health — data deletion & log retention: proposed exception and process
messages:
From: John Davis <john.davis@equinoxhealth.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Data deletion / log retention for PHI — need specifics and exception request

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the SOC 2 packet — the security team at Equinox had a couple of follow-ups specific to our PHI handling requirements. Two main asks:  

1) We need confirmation of the exact retention windows for the following artifacts when using Redwood Hosted API (default): request logs, inference payloads/response traces, and audit logs. Please include both the retention period and whether backups/snapshots may extend retention beyond the primary window.

2) Equinox must keep the right to have customer-requested deletion of all inference payloads and associated traces within 30 days of a deletion request. Can Redwood commit to a contractual exception for this account (or point me to the process and SLAs for such an exception)? We also need to understand if there are any residual logs kept for debugging that contain customer-provided text and how they are purged.

We will likely need a short addendum in the MSA if this is possible. Please loop in any folks on your side who manage retention exceptions.

Appreciate a short summary and any evidence (SOC2/Audit notes) you can share.

Best,
John Davis\Security Operations\Equinox Health

---
Attachments: none
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: John Davis <john.davis@equinoxhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Data deletion / log retention for PHI — need specifics and exception request

John — thanks for the clear asks. High-level answers below; I've attached our SOC 2 attestation and a concise retention table for quick reference. I've also cc'd Marcus (Legal ops) to start the conversation about a contract addendum if Equinox needs a stricter deletion SLA.

Quick summary (Hosted API default):
- Request logs (request metadata, timestamps, IPs): retained for 90 days by default. Backups/snapshots that include logs are retained for up to 180 days during disaster recovery windows; those backups are rotated and ephemeral.
- Inference payloads & response traces (customer prompt & generated tokens): by default, Redwood does not persist full inference payloads beyond immediate processing except for short-term traces used for debugging. Traces are retained up to 30 days and are accessible only to SRE/ops in controlled workflows.
- Audit logs (admin changes, API key activity, route changes): retained 365 days and stored in immutable logs for compliance review.

Customer-specific exception options we support:
1) Hosted contractual exception: we can add a data-retention addendum that shortens backup windows and enforces 30-day deletion for inference traces. This requires Legal review and a scoped SLA (we typically exclude forensic snapshots and narrow certain debug trace exceptions).
2) Dedicated / Private deployment: for customers requiring stricter controls (e.g., guaranteed deletion within 30 days with no platform-managed backups), Dedicated capacity or Private deployment is recommended; retention windows are configurable in those modes.

Residual logs: We do keep ephemeral debug logs that may contain redacted snippets; for exceptions we can implement an enhanced purge procedure and config the platform to disable debug trace capture for your tenant.

Next steps I propose:
- Marcus can share our standard addendum template (if Legal agrees).
- If Equinox prefers, we can open a short SOW for a dedicated retention configuration in Dedicated/Private.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_Attestation_2025.pdf; Redwood_Audit_Logs_Retention_Table.csv

Thanks — I'll wait for your preference on addendum vs. dedicated deployment and we'll route it through Marcus/Legal.

Sincerely,
Soojin Lee\Product Security Manager\Redwood Inference
Support: security@redwoodinference.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 08:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Data deletion / log retention for PHI — Equinox asking for 30-day deletion exception

Mark / Laura — forwarding Equinox's request. Key asks: 30-day deletion of inference payloads/traces and confirmation that backups won't extend retention beyond that. John is leaning toward staying on Hosted but wants contractual assurance.

My read: we can offer a Hosted addendum that: 1) sets trace retention to <=30 days, 2) explicitly excludes forensic snapshots (they still exist for platform recovery) but commits to not include customer data in those snapshots to the extent operationally feasible, and 3) adds an explicit purge workflow with a verified audit log for the deletion request.

Questions for Legal/Compliance:
- Is there language we can use to limit scope so we're not guaranteeing elimination of DR snapshots created before a deletion request?
- What sort of verification evidence will we commit (audit event with timestamp / internal ticket id)?

I've drafted suggested addendum bullets below — happy to iterate. If you're ok, I'll propose the language to John + the security team and request a short review call.

Draft addendum bullets (very high level):
- Redwood agrees to purge all customer inference traces and related short-term debug logs within 30 days of an authorized deletion request initiated by Equinox.
- Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts to exclude customer-identifiable data from disaster recovery snapshots created after the deletion request; snapshots that pre-date the request are explicitly scoped out.
- Redwood will provide a deletion verification artifact (audit event id, timestamp, and ticket reference) within five business days of completion.

LMK if you want the redline — I can prepare for Legal review.

— Soojin
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: John Davis <john.davis@equinoxhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 16:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Data deletion / log retention for PHI — proposed addendum and next steps

John — thanks for the patience. Per our internal review (cc'd Marcus + Laura), we can support the 30-day deletion requirement for inference traces in Hosted with a scoped addendum. Summary of what we can commit and what remains out of scope:  

What Redwood will commit to (Hosted addendum):
- Purge window: Redwood will purge all customer inference traces and debug traces containing customer-provided text within 30 calendar days of an authorized deletion request submitted by an Equinox authorized admin.
- Verification: Redwood will provide a deletion verification artifact (audit event ID, deletion timestamp, and internal ticket reference) within 5 business days of the purge completion.
- Backup handling: Redwood will not use backups or snapshots to retain customer inference traces beyond the 30-day purge window to the extent operationally feasible; snapshots created prior to the deletion request are out of scope.

Out of scope / limitations:
- Forensic snapshots or platform-level disaster recovery snapshots that pre-date the deletion request cannot be guaranteed to have been purged; we will, however, label and segregate customer data in our backup processes and document the timelines.
- If Equinox requires absolute elimination from all possible platform backups regardless of pre-date, we will recommend Dedicated or Private deployment as the contractual path.

Next steps:
1) Marcus will send a short retention addendum draft for Legal review (DocuSign link attached).
2) If Equinox signs, we will schedule a short onboarding call to configure trace capture flags for your tenant and confirm the deletion workflow (estimated 5 business days after signed addendum).
